mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC of FEDFUNDS against 20-day S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 236.0 indicates persistent inflationary pressure that triggers a central bank tightening response, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets price in higher interest rates.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 236.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profit growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE rising and PAYEMS falling) fails to predict negative returns: when the condition is met, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC of the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs suppress corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for housing and related goods, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC of HOUST against 20-day S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing output level below 104.0 (INDPRO) signals a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 104.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer spending and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS rising and HOUST rising) fails to predict positive returns: when the condition is met, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC of the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a high unemployment regime (UNRATE above 5.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as weak labor markets suppress consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.
